title: Warm water on real silicon: does energy-optimal control make AI waste heat reusable, and what does a heat-reuse supply floor cost?
research_question: With clock sensitivity, leakage-temperature slope and voltage-frequency shape taken from a real GPU instead of placeholders, how warm does energy-optimal (lag-aware joint) control run the coolant, how much of the rejected heat becomes reusable (return water >= 45 C), and what does forcing a 40 C supply floor cost in energy, safety and service?
hypothesis: Conditions: 2 parameter worlds (registry; measured) x 2 supply floors (none, i.e. 12 C; 40 C) x 2 plants (quasi-steady; 150 kg loop, 0.25 K/min) x 3 scenarios (S1 20 C, S3 35 C, S4 8 C ambient). H1: without a floor, joint_lag's time-averaged supply temperature is at least 10 K higher in the measured world than in the registry world, in every scenario and plant. H2: without a floor, in the measured world joint_lag makes at least 50% of rejected heat reusable in S1 and S4 with the quasi-steady plant, while in the registry world it makes less than 20% reusable there. H3: the 40 C floor raises joint_lag's energy per successful task by less than 0.5% (95% CI upper bound) in the measured world in every scenario and plant, and the floor's penalty is larger in the registry world than in the measured world in every scenario and plant (seed-paired difference of penalties, 95% CI above 0). H4: joint_lag records zero chip-seconds above 80 C in all 24 conditions. H5: steady-state joint exceeds 80 C in at least one condition with the 150 kg loop.
null_hypothesis: Real-silicon parameters change neither the energy-optimal supply temperature nor the cost of warm-water operation.
controlled_variables: registry values for everything not listed in the world
reuse threshold t_reuse_min = 45 C (registry, class F)
baseline: registry world within each floor, plant and scenario; no floor within each world
configuration: Worlds: {'registry': {}, 'measured': {'beta_compute': 0.983, 'beta_memory': 0.0, 'kappa_leak': 0.02, 'p_leak_ref': 27.42, 'v_min_ratio': 0.78, 'vf_knee': 0.805}}. Floors: {'nofloor': {'t_sup_min': 12.0}, 'floor40': {'t_sup_min': 40.0}}. Plants: {'quasi': {'loop_mass_kg': 0.0, 'tsup_ramp_K_per_min': 0.0}, 'dyn150': {'loop_mass_kg': 150.0, 'tsup_ramp_K_per_min': 0.25}}. Measured-world V-f and leakage from data/calibration/M001_vf_fit.json (rms shape error 0.016 of top-clock power vs 0.049 for the registry linear form).
evaluation_criteria: T_sup_mean_C and reuse fractions as seed means over 5 seeds; energy as paired relative differences with 95% t-CI; floor penalty = E_per_success(floor40)/E_per_success(nofloor) - 1 per seed.
known_limitations: Heat counts as reusable when the water leaving the loop is at or above 45 C; there is no heat customer, price or seasonal demand. The measured world transfers shapes from one 250 W consumer card to a 600 W-class simulated accelerator (class E). Leakage slope from a 4 K window. Ambient temperature is constant within a run. 5 seeds.
disclosure: Written before E011's results were seen and before any E012 cell ran. Known: E009 and E010 results; the voltage-floor fit (v_min_ratio 0.78, vf_knee 0.805, p_leak_ref re-matched to 27.42 W); one exploratory E011 run (see E011). The T_sup_mean_C metric is added to the simulator after this spec is committed and before E012 runs; it changes no other output.
data_collection: Simulator outputs written to the append-only SQLite store; every metric labelled with provenance; per-run config SHA-256 and code SHA-256 recorded; time series for selected seeds.
statistics: Paired by seed (identical workload realisation across levels). Per-seed relative difference d=(A-B)/B; mean with two-sided 95% Student-t CI.
